Here's a one-page sheet you can glance at on the ride.

[Image: A single portrait page titled "Bottleneck & Tote Flow Cheat Sheet", with a left-to-right process flow at the top: three boxes (Station A, Station B, Station C) joined by arrows, each labeled with its capacity in units/hour. The slowest box is outlined in red and tagged "BOTTLENECK = min(capacities)".

Below it, a two-column grid of formula cards:

LEFT COLUMN (Bottleneck)
- Process capacity = min(capacity of each step)
- Capacity per step = (# of workers or machines) / (time per unit)
- Utilization = actual output / capacity
- Cycle time = 1 / throughput rate

RIGHT COLUMN (Tote flow)
- Throughput (R) = totes completed per hour
- Flow time (T) = time a tote spends in the system
- Inventory (I) = totes in the system (WIP)
- Little's Law: I = R x T (rearrange: T = I / R, R = I / T)
- Takt time = available time / demand

Bottom strip in a yellow box: "Check units first (per min vs per hour). Output can't exceed the bottleneck. Speeding up a non-bottleneck step does nothing."]

Quick example to lock it in: if the stations run at 120, 90 and 150 totes/hour, the system maxes out at 90/hour. If 45 totes are in the system, flow time is 45 / 90 = 0.5 hours.

If Dr. Ashby's notes use different symbols, tell me and I'll relabel the sheet. Good luck on the midterm!
